speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (a) how many ex-teachers have rejoined the education service last year; (b) how many of these teachers have resigned as employees of independent schools to rejoin the service; and (c) how are the teachers' experience and skills that are developed in the time after the teachers left service recognised when they rejoin the service.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there an existing policy to welcome the ex-teachers to rejoin the Education Service, rather than the ad hoc kind of re-application by the teachers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And would the Ministry formulate a clear framework to recognise the ex-teachers' experience and skills, developed in the time they have left the Service?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Ministry then publicise this framework so that ex-teachers with developed experience could be attracted back to teaching?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I am not so sure whether I could address the Member's question in terms of a policy to welcome ex-teachers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I mean, the applications are certainly welcomed and the skills are certainly valued.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The ability for these officers to apply for those jobs is certainly well known.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I welcome any suggestions you might have about how we might do that better.
